key_insight: Among cancer patients in Northwest Russia, receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose before the landmark date was associated with markedly better overall survival.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest vaccination may be an important protective factor for cancer patients, alongside stage and treatment status, but the results are observational rather than proof of causation.
method: Population-based retrospective cohort using cancer registry, vaccination records, and CT-linked AI data.
Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox models compared vaccinated vs unvaccinated patients.
Landmark analyses were used to reduce immortal time bias, with a sensitivity analysis at a later date.
evidence_signal: In 1,136 patients in the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with higher 3-year OS (80.3% vs 45.7%) and a lower adjusted mortality hazard (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.64).
watch_item: Vaccinated patients had earlier-stage disease and were less likely to be on active treatment, so residual confounding and selection bias may influence the association.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
